clue.text: First of clues across clued as 'Irish salt-marsh'

indicators.note: first of a word means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of clues

indicators.note: to clue a word is to disguise it, so these letters appear in disguised order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter's note on the puzzle: the opening across clue is to define the word as an Irish salt-marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an instruction about this very puzzle, where 1 across is the first across clue; really it is wordplay, with 'clued' signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Corcass is an Irish word, in Chambers, for a salt-marsh or low-lying marshy land beside a river.

clue.text: Cactus bursting out, and pain's involved with it

indicators.note: something bursting flies apart, so its letters scatter into a new order
involved means tangled up together, so the second set of letters is mixed in as well

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, the possessive 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A prickly cactus breaks into flower, and handling it is painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With it' tells you the letters of pain join those of out in a single jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Opuntia is the genus of prickly-pear cacti, with flat jointed pads covered in spines.

clue.text: Rhythmical stuff, grand in south Asian piece

indicators.note: the single letter is placed inside the piece of music that follows

parts.note: a raga is a traditional melodic form in Indian music
G is short for grand, as in a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A rhythmic composition with an impressive passage in an Indian piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The G goes after the first G of RAGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragga is a style of dance music derived from reggae, built on heavy electronic rhythms.

clue.text: Sweet cake recipe — one reducing numbers restricts it

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the outer word closes around the other

parts.note: a culler thins out a herd or flock, cutting its numbers
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A baker on a diet keeps a cake recipe under tight control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points back to recipe, which the culler encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruller is a sweet twisted doughnut-like cake fried in fat, popular in North America.

clue.text: Luminance being admitted rescues towering rainforests

indicators.note: in a down light, towering means rising up, so the letters read from bottom to top
something admitted is let in, so this letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: to rescue is to save
L is the symbol for luminance

explanation.surface: Letting light in through the canopy saves the tall rainforest trees.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes between the V and E of SAVES, and the result is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Selva is the term for the dense equatorial rainforest of the Amazon basin.

clue.text: Sherry casks filling señora with local cheer

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so the cheer goes within the title

parts.note: Sra is the abbreviation of señora
olé is the Spanish shout of approval, local to the land of sherry

explanation.surface: A Spanish lady is cheered by full barrels of sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' ties the cheer to Spain, the home of sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: A solera is a tiered system of casks in which sherry is blended, younger wine topping up older.

clue.text: You may see me involved in much impishness

definitions.text: You may see me involved in much impishness

indicators.note: something involved in a phrase is wrapped up inside it, so the letters lie within the next two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A creature boasts that it can be spotted wherever there is plenty of mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: CHIMP sits inside 'much impishness', and a chimp is the very picture of impishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimpanzees are famous for playful, mischievous antics, so a chimp is what you would expect to find in impish behaviour.

clue.text: Erstwhile black personification of youth, note

parts.note: Hebe was the Greek goddess of youth
N is short for note

explanation.surface: An old-time youth idol in a black outfit is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erstwhile' marks the definition as an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Heben is an old form of ebony, the wood whose deep black colour gave its name to the shade.

clue.text: I strain to retain first of ingredients in list

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: retaining means holding something inside, so the sieve word keeps the letter within it

parts.note: temse is an old word for a sieve, and to temse is to strain

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of ingredients

explanation.surface: A cook sieves the first ingredients while writing out a shopping list.
explanation.walkthrough: TEMSE is a Chambers word for a sieve; the I goes after its M.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set things out one by one, as in a list.

clue.text: Club, first in table, displaying worth

parts.note: a meri is a Maori war club

indicators.note: first in a word means its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of table

explanation.surface: A sports club tops the league table, proving its quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a team, but it is the Maori weapon MERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit and worth both mean the quality of deserving praise or reward.

clue.text: Rubbish etc churned out in the papers. Guardian may be one

indicators.note: the mixed letters go inside the word for newspapers

parts.note: the press means newspapers collectively

indicators.note: churning stirs things vigorously, so the letters of these words are mixed up

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plenty of rubbish gets printed in the papers, and the Guardian newspaper may be guilty of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital G makes the Guardian look like the newspaper, which fits the surface; it is any female guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: A protectress is a woman who protects someone, so a female guardian may be one.

clue.text: Critic in review anti, ruffled

indicators.note: a text in review is being revised and reworked, so the following letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, every letter of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A reviewer who is against everything and easily ruffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruffled' looks like the anagram signal, but it belongs to the letters; 'in review' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic is someone who points out shortcomings, which is exactly what a fault-finder does.

clue.text: Specific gravity gauge showing old measurement in jungly tree area

indicators.note: one part is placed inside the scrambled letters of the following words
a jungly mass is tangled and overgrown, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
Chambers lists OM as an abbreviation for Old Measurement

explanation.surface: Someone measuring specific gravity in a dense stretch of forest, using an old-fashioned unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the Chambers spelling of areometer, with the extra A of its Greek root.
explanation.definitionFit: An araeometer is a hydrometer, an instrument floated in a liquid to read its density relative to water.

clue.text: One divining gold, unrefined stuff, from cane

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
gur is unrefined sugar made from cane juice in India

explanation.surface: A dowser seeks out gold while chewing on raw sugar cane.
explanation.walkthrough: GUR is a Chambers word for coarse Indian cane sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: An augur was a Roman official who foretold events from omens, so he is a diviner.

clue.text: Member of team reconditioning boiler

indicators.note: reconditioning means overhauling and rebuilding, so the next word's letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A plumber on the works team is busy refitting a boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Team' suggests a crew of workmen; it is a football side.
explanation.definitionFit: A libero is a football sweeper, the free defender who plays behind the back line of a team.

clue.text: Ready for a serious fight, loaded gun held close

indicators.note: loaded is slang for drunk, and a drunken word staggers into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
someone held close is cherished, loved

explanation.surface: A fighter is primed for trouble, keeping a loaded gun close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded gun' reads as a weapon, but 'loaded' is the signal to rearrange GUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers who take off their gloves fight bare-knuckled, so ungloved describes someone ready for a fight in earnest.

clue.text: Uniat spread, on replacing central mass

indicators.note: one item takes the place of another sitting in the very middle of the word before it

parts.note: Marmite is a British yeast-extract spread eaten on toast
taken as written
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A churchgoer of the Eastern rite smears something on toast, perhaps after replacing the middle of a large heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniat' needs no anagram despite 'spread' beside it: spread is a noun here, the food. Uniat churches are Eastern churches that accept the Pope's authority.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maronites of Lebanon are an Eastern church in communion with Rome, and Uniat is the term for such churches.

clue.text: Norman (say) coming over ousts leader of Britons in this country

indicators.note: coming over suggests turning head over heels, so the name is read from its end back to its start
to oust is to throw out, so that letter is removed from the reversed name

parts.note: Norman Tebbit, a Conservative cabinet minister under Margaret Thatcher

indicators.note: a leader stands at the front, so only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of Britons

explanation.surface: A Norman invader crosses the Channel and throws the British chief out of power here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norman (say)' looks like an invader of 1066; it is Norman Tebbit, the Thatcher-era Tory politician. TIBBET loses one B.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is a Himalayan land, and 'this country' points to the answer itself as the country being named.

clue.text: One of an isomeric pair saving an elderly person sine die

indicators.note: sine is Latin for without, so the elderly person comes without the letters of die

parts.note: saving means except, as does but
taken as written
an oldie is an old person

explanation.surface: A chemist preserves an old person's remains indefinitely, adjourning matters sine die.
explanation.walkthrough: Sine die is a Latin legal phrase meaning indefinitely; here it is read literally as 'without DIE'.
explanation.definitionFit: Butanol is an alcohol whose molecule can be arranged in more than one way, so its forms are isomers.

clue.text: Count, almost 100, without extras

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Count Basie, the American jazz pianist and bandleader
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone tallies up to nearly a hundred, leaving out the extras as a cricket scorer might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb; it is the title of the jazz bandleader Count Basie.
explanation.definitionFit: A basic model or package is the plain version, with no add-ons or optional extras.

clue.text: Bird's bare patches more appropriate on centre of dial

parts.note: apter means more apt

indicators.note: the centre of a four-letter word is its two middle letters

parts.note: the two middle letters of dial

explanation.surface: A bird's bald spots look all the better around the middle of a clock face.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Apteria are the bare strips of a bird's skin between the tracts where feathers grow.

clue.text: The old withdraw from sin dodging place where it often occurs

indicators.note: dodging means darting this way and that, so the letters move about

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
hell is where sinners end up, so sin is rife there

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned folk retreat from wickedness by avoiding dens of iniquity.
explanation.walkthrough: Inshell is Shakespeare's word, in Coriolanus, for drawing in as a snail draws into its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: To inshell is to draw back into a shell, which is to withdraw.

clue.text: Heart of heuch in remote, deserted Scotland's well-liked

indicators.note: the selected letter is set inside the word that follows

parts.note: remote means far away

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, the one in the middle of the five

parts.note: the middle letter of heuch, a Scots word for a crag or steep bank
D is an abbreviation for deserted

explanation.surface: A lonely Scottish crag far from anywhere is fondly regarded by the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: FAURD is a Scots form of favoured; the U goes inside FAR, then D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Faurd is the Scots form of favoured, and someone favoured is regarded with liking and approval.

clue.text: Decorator in company, type that's close to English

indicators.note: the decorator sits inside the abbreviation for company

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation of company
an icer decorates cakes

explanation.surface: A painter-decorator working for a firm that sets type near the English border.
explanation.walkthrough: English is the name of an old type size, so the definition is about printing, not nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero is a continental unit of type size, very near the old English size of type.

clue.text: Adventurous fish one catches round middle of beach

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to nab is to catch

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter

parts.note: the middle letter of beach

explanation.surface: A daring fish is caught by someone wandering about the middle of the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: NABS goes round the A from beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabas is the climbing perch, a fish that can leave water and is said to climb trees, so it is adventurous.

clue.text: Crisp entrecote only partly consumed

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the answer is a run of letters within them

parts.note: the letters straddle the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A steak with a crispy crust is left half-eaten on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crisp' looks like a description of the steak; its tail end starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or energy that has been spent is used up, which is what consumed means here.

clue.text: Yellowish cuckoo inert, frost-bound

indicators.note: something bound by frost is held fast inside it, so the frozen word wraps round the others

parts.note: frost is a coating of ice

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the next word's letters go haywire

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sallow cuckoo sits motionless, trapped in the frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' looks like the bird in a wintry scene; it signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Icterine comes from the Greek for jaundice, and describes yellowish colouring, as in the icterine warbler.

clue.text: Chestnut, one in traditional hunt

parts.note: ch is the racing abbreviation for a chestnut horse
an ace is a one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A chestnut horse takes part in a hunt of the old-fashioned kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chestnut' looks like the tree or an old joke; it is the horse colour, abbreviated as in racing form guides.
explanation.definitionFit: Chace is an old spelling of chase, the pursuit of game, so 'traditional' signals the archaic form.

clue.text: Without siblings, seeing one's first off, possibly?

definitions.note: loosely: the first-born has no older siblings

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements of the remaining letters
with its first off, the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written, before losing its first letter

explanation.surface: An only child wonders whether a sibling seeing them first might go off.
explanation.walkthrough: Eigne is a legal term from French aîné for the eldest-born, who for a time has no siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: Eigne means first-born or eldest, and a first-born child begins life with no brothers or sisters.

clue.text: Big electronics company producing record issue

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: A major electronics firm releases a new recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a release of a record; it means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Epson is a large Japanese maker of printers, projectors and other electronic equipment.

clue.text: Jellyfish making one jump, as before, in pain

indicators.note: the first two pieces are placed inside the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a pain
a means one
lep is an old and dialect form of leap; 'as before' marks it as dated

explanation.surface: A jellyfish sting makes a swimmer leap, just as last time, in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' looks like repetition of the jump; it marks an old form of the word, as Chambers labels archaisms.
explanation.definitionFit: Acalephe is an old Chambers name for a jellyfish, from the Greek for nettle, after its sting.

clue.text: Show to encourage girl that's lost heart in Hamlet?

indicators.note: the shortened word is placed inside the following one

parts.note: Hamlet was a prince of Denmark, so he is an example of a Dane; the question mark flags the example

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letters of the word go, leaving only its ends

parts.note: taken as written, before its middle two letters go

explanation.surface: A performance meant to cheer up Ophelia, the heartbroken girl in Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: The heartbroken girl in Hamlet calls Ophelia to mind, but the girl is just the word, and Hamlet stands for his nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle a reward, like a carrot before a donkey, is to hold it out as an inducement to act.

clue.text: Barristers clearing every second character — they're upbeat

definitions.note: a clause standing for a plural noun: things that are upbeats

indicators.note: clearing alternate characters means throwing out every other one and keeping the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Lawyers who are acquitting every other defendant are in a cheerful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upbeat' looks like cheerful; it is the musical term. Arses is the plural of arsis.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an arsis is the unaccented upbeat of a bar, so arses are upbeats.

clue.text: Action or reaction? Not at all (10, two words)

indicators.note: putting letters into action sets them moving, so they rearrange themselves

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asked whether something is an action or a reaction, the speaker denies both.
explanation.walkthrough: The question looks like physics; the words after 'Action' are the letters to rearrange. E contrario is Latin for 'from the contrary'.
explanation.definitionFit: E contrario is Latin for on the contrary, a phrase used as an emphatic denial.

clue.text: As part of exposure, letters released

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words that follow, a run of their letters

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: Letters made public as part of an exposé of some scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like correspondence; the answer runs across it.
explanation.definitionFit: A property that is relet has been let again, released to a new tenant.

clue.text: Fellow in oil's rolling, a Turkish dynast

indicators.note: the word for fellow goes inside the scrambled letters
rolling things tumble over, so the letters of the oil phrase are mixed

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man rolling in oil money, like a wealthy Ottoman ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmanli means of the dynasty of Osman, founder of the Ottoman empire, so an Osmanli is a member of that dynasty.
